title: Play a slow 4/4 rock-ballad groove with two sticks on an electronic drum kit: accented hi-hat, snare backbeat, tom fill
instruction: Play this groove on the drum kit with the stick in each hand, at 75 beats per minute, counting 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 &. Bars 1 to 3: hit the hi-hat on every count, loud on the numbers and soft on the ands, and the snare loud on 2 and 4 together with the hi-hat. Bar 4: the same up to 3 &, then only the tom, on 4 and on 4 &. End with the hi-hat and snare together on 1 of the next bar. Let each stroke come straight off the pad; at the end hold both sticks still, clear of the kit.
context: Two sticks strike two pads at once, one hand alternates loud and soft strokes, the other leaves the snare for the tom mid-bar and is back on the beat, and every stroke must come cleanly off the pad. Unlike xylophone keys struck one at a time, strokes are timed, paired and accented; unlike keyboard dynamics (TK-DPZS6F), each is a held stick's impact. This is the basic rock groove most people have watched drummers play: one stick keeps eighths on the hi-hat while the other lands the backbeat, and on 2 and 4 both sound together. Loudness comes from how fast the tip meets the pad, so the hi-hat hand changes its stroke height every count. A stick in a parallel gripper has no loose fulcrum: a bouncing stroke sends extra notes, a stroke left on the pad counts as a fault, and a hard one can turn the stick in the grip. Nothing is read or chosen: the groove is in the instruction. The kit's own MIDI records each pad, time and loudness. The bass drum is a foot's part and is not played.
setup: Units mm. x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the robot's left, z up from the table top. Two YAM arms with parallel grippers, bases at y = +305 and y = -305, at the near edge of a wooden table top that reaches at least y = -600 and y = +600 and at least 800 forward of the bases; one overhead camera and one camera on each wrist (320 x 176). The arms start at a playing pose (its joint angles are in the package's README): each gripper points sideways toward the robot's centre line and holds one Vic Firth American Classic 5A hickory drumstick with a wood tip (406 long, 14.4 across, about 50 g; weigh it), its finger pads closed on the stick's upper and lower sides at a tape mark 135 mm from the butt, the stick at right angles to the gripper and its tip forward, 80 above its pad. The kit is three pads of an Alesis Nitro Max electronic drum kit at their real sizes, set for open-handed playing: the hi-hat in front of the left arm, the snare and the tom in front of the right arm, with the hi-hat left of the snare and higher, as on a right-handed kit. (1) The 10-inch hi-hat pad: centre (500, +180), its edge 120 above the table, level; its foot controller lies on the floor with a 2 kg weight (for example a bag of sand) on its footboard, so the hi-hat stays closed. (2) The 10-inch dual-zone mesh snare pad: head centre (500, -140), head 100 above the table, tilted 5 degrees toward the robot. (3) One 8-inch single-zone mesh tom pad (the kit's tom 3, in the floor-tom place right of the snare): head centre (500, -420), head 90 above the table, tilted 5 degrees toward the robot; its rim reaches y = -534. Gaps in plan: hi-hat edge to snare rim 54, snare rim to tom rim 27. Each pad is held by the kit's own clamp and L-arm on one of the kit's rack tubes, which lies along the table's far side, clamped with two C-clamps; each pad's place is marked with tape. The kit's other pads, kick pad and pedal are not used and are off the table. The drum module is on the floor behind the table, at factory settings and kit 1, except: each pad's threshold (THR) is set so that a stick pivoting loosely at its tape mark, its tip let fall from 10 mm above the pad's centre, does not trigger, and from 20 mm does; crosstalk (CRO) is set so that ten loud snare strokes trigger no other pad; the velocity curve (CUR) and the pads' MIDI note numbers are recorded with the trial. Its USB port goes to a computer that records MIDI (any DAW or MIDI logger). Cables run under the pads to the far edge. Nothing else is on the table. Real trial only, not simulated: a phone on a stand beside the table's right edge, level with the pads and facing them, films the trial for the video checks. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Every hit is a MIDI note-on: in a real trial from the drum module's USB MIDI output, in simulation from the hit log written as a MIDI file; the same scorer reads both. In simulation a hit is a held stick (no other part of the robot, and no stick that has left its gripper) meeting a pad's playing surface with an impulse of at least 0.003 N s while moving toward it at 0.5 m/s or more, read every physics step (240 Hz); a stick must leave a pad (2 mm, 2 steps) before it can hit it again; the tom pad has one zone, so a stick on its rim plays the tom, while the snare's rim is a zone of its own. The scorer merges note-ons on the same pad less than 40 ms apart, then fits one tempo (60 to 90 bpm) and one start to the hits. A written note is played when a hit on its pad lies within 50 ms of the note's fitted time; that difference is its timing error. A pair (hi-hat and snare on the same count, 8 pairs) is together when both notes are played by the two different sticks within 40 ms of each other. Extra or wrong hits: a hit that plays no note (a rim, the wrong pad, a second hit, a hit after the last note) or a gripper or arm striking a pad (in simulation, any contact over 2 N); up to four hi-hat hits in the bar before the first note are a count-in and do not count. Accent rule: the hi-hat notes on the numbers average at least 25 MIDI velocity above those on the ands, each louder than the ands either side of it, and the snare notes average at least 25 above the hi-hat ands. Clean end: after the last pair, no more hits, and within 3 s both sticks held with their tips at least 50 mm from every pad for 1 s. Score: 1.0 if all 41 notes are played, all 8 pairs together, the RMS timing error is at most 25 ms, the fitted tempo is 71 to 79 bpm, the accent rule holds, there is at most one extra or wrong hit and the end is clean; 0.9 if all of that holds except the accent rule; 0.75 if at least 37 notes are played, 7 pairs together, the RMS error is at most 35 ms and there are at most 3 extra or wrong hits; 0.5 if at least 31 notes and 5 pairs, with at most 3 extra or wrong hits; 0.25 if at least 16 notes, with at most 3 extra or wrong hits; otherwise 0. A gripper or arm striking a pad caps the score at 0.5, and a stick resting on a pad for 0.5 s or more caps it at 0.75; in a real trial a pad knocked 10 mm off its mark scores 0 (the simulated pads are fixed). In a real trial, which stick struck at the 8 pairs, resting, gripper or arm strikes, dropped sticks and the clean end are read from the trial video, and a note sent by a gripper, an arm or a dropped stick plays no note. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the end is clean with the score at 1.0. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9, 1.0.
reset_notes: Start a new MIDI recording. With both arms at the start pose, put each stick between its gripper's finger pads at the tape mark (pads on the stick's upper and lower sides, tip forward) and close the gripper. Check each pad against its tape marks and angle, the weight on the hi-hat controller, and the module on kit 1 with the recorded settings. Nothing is consumed; replace a stick whose tip is chipped. In simulation: seed 0, no jitter; the sticks start in the closed grippers and settle for 0.5 s before the first step.
fidelity: No sound is simulated. A hit is a held stick meeting a pad at 0.5 m/s or more with an impulse of at least 0.003 N s, read every physics step (240 Hz) with a 40 ms mask, and written as MIDI (velocity from tip speed on an estimated curve). Pads are fixed and rigid, restitution 0.7 (estimated); the hi-hat is fixed closed; no bass drum. Sticks are rigid, 50 g, held by friction only (0.8), and turn and slide in the grip. Audio is added from the hits.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (1,200 steps; gripped both sticks, then opened the grippers and dropped them; no hit); demo: 1.0 (305 steps; 41/41 notes, RMS 3 ms, pairs within 8 ms, 75.0 bpm). Same fixed scene, hit rule and MIDI scorer.
